newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan to push Israel to ease Palestinian siege.
newsitem.headline: Jordan to push Israel to ease Palestinian siege.

text.p: Jordan will urge Israel at summit talks on Wednesday to ease sanctions imposed on Palestinians after suicide bombers killed 14 people in Jerusalem last month, Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah said on Tuesday.
Tarawnah said King Hussein would stress to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu his support for Palestinian calls for an easing of the two-week blockade on their territories.
Jordan would also call for a full resumption of the peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians, Tarawnah said.
"There has been some relaxation of some of the measures... But we are not satisfied," he told Reuters. "Many of the steps were totally unjustified."

Israel has lifted inner closures between some of the scattered self-ruled Palestinian towns in the West Bank and allowed relief trucks into Gaza but an overall ban on Palestinians entering Israel remains intact.
Tarawnah said Israel should also revoke a decision to block transfer of customs revenues to the Palestinian Authority, which he said was "totally illegal".
Netanyahu's meeting with King Hussein in the Red Sea resort of Aqaba will be his first with an Arab leader since suicide bombers plunged Middle East peace negotiations into crisis.

U.S. envoy Dennis Ross was shuttling between Netanyahu and Arafat on Tuesday in an attempt to restore security cooperation between the two sides, which Netanyahu says must come before any resumption of talks on expanding Palestinian self-rule.
Arafat has said he is making a "100 percent" effort to arrest militants opposed to his interim peace deal with Israel. Netanyahu said he was still "looking for results" from the Palestinians.
"The main focus is a resumption of negotiations on all issues... We will be pushing for Israel to consider (Palestinian President Yasser) Arafat a full partner and not an enemy," Tarawnah said.

Talks had already been deadlocked since March when Israel began work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. Palestinians say Israel is also stalling on previously agreed steps to release prisoners, open sea and air ports in Gaza and create a 'safe passage' between the Gaza Strip and West Bank.

Tarawnah said security cooperation was a "cornerstone" of the peace process but added it was not the only issue on the table, and he warned that Arafat might not be able to meet all of Netanyahu's security demands.
"He should consider Arafat's position. You cannot ask sometimes impossible things."

King Hussein, who sent his brother Crown Prince Hassan on an apparently fruitless trip to Jerusalem last week for talks with Netanyahu, has expressed bewilderment about his own meetings with the Israeli prime minister.

"We talk openly. We seem to have the same view... But then things do not seem to continue in a path that you could recognise, or identify with what you have spoken about," he told an interviewer last month.
